Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — August payrolls data, July revision
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Fed September 15-16 meeting rate decision, mortgage market stress
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    August NFP came in at +162K, a strong beat vs. the +56K consensus and a sharp reversal from July's upwardly revised +21K. Unemployment held at 4.1%. Despite the beat, rate hike odds for the Sep 15-16 Fed meeting eased to ~52% from 63.2% after Fed Governor Waller signaled openness to holding rates steady if inflation data cooperates. Rising Treasury yields have pushed the 30-yr mortgage rate to a 1-year high of 6.71%, adding pressure to the housing market. Background context includes labor market drag from an oil price shock and supply chain disruptions tied to a U.S.-Iran conflict.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — covers NFP, unemployment, Fed rate path, Treasury yields, mortgage rates, and CME FedWatch pricing directly

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 65 (meaningfully relevant — rate hike is live and on the table)
Probability of increase: 52% (per CME FedWatch as of article date)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 60 (relevant — Waller's comments lean toward a hold contingent on inflation data)
Probability of holding: 48% (inverse of CME hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — no discussion of cuts whatsoever)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -15 (Slightly dovish lean at the margin — the NFP beat is hawkish on its own, but Waller's late Thursday comments actively walked back hike expectations, pulling market pricing from 63.2% to 52%; the net latest signal is a modest dovish tilt despite strong labor data)
